title: Protocol for analyzing γδ T cells from the vagina of diet-induced obese mice using single-cell RNA sequencing and flow cytometry
protocol: Draw up 50 μl of chilled D-PBS (without calcium and magnesium) using an autoclaved 200 μL pipette tip.
Gently insert the end of the pipette tip into the vaginal opening of the mouse.
Push the piston of the pipette to wash the inside of the mouse vagina, collecting withdrawn fluid as vaginal lavage.
Repeat washing procedures until the withdrawn fluid is clear.
Inject 100 μl MPA solution subcutaneously into the back of a mouse.
Inject HSV-2 intravaginally five to seven days after MPA injection.
Monitor the estrus cycle of mice after MPA injection.
Check vaginal lavage to determine diestrus induction time point.
Dilute HSV-2 stock in D-PBS (without calcium and magnesium) to obtain a final concentration of 10^6 pfu/mL.
Wash the vaginal tract of mice with chilled D-PBS.
Inject 10 μL diluted virus into the vagina using a micropipette tip.
Monitor body weight and score infection severity daily.
Euthanize mice before reaching a moribund state.
Euthanize the mouse by CO2 inhalation and sanitize with 70% ethanol.
Remove the abdominal skin and expose the abdominal muscle.
Remove the fat tissue under the pelvis.
Dissociate the mouse vagina.
Cut the abdominal skin of the mouse and expose the peritoneal muscle.
Pull the skin to the tail to expose the pelvis and remove fat tissue.
Make an incision in the abdominal side of the pelvis with scissors.
Open the incision to expose the vaginal tissue.
When the vaginal tissue is exposed, identify the urethra located on the vagina.
Carefully remove the urethra from the vaginal tissue without rupturing the bladder.
Cut out the vulva from the perineum.
Pull the vagina and vulva orthogonal to the rectum to separate the vagina from the rectum.
Fully separate the vagina from the rectum until the cervix is visible.
Excise vaginal tissue from the cervix and excise the vulva.
Remove the urethra from the vaginal tissue without rupturing the bladder.
Cut out the vulva from the perineum carefully.
Pull the vagina orthogonal to the rectum to dissociate it from the rectal tissue.
Fully dissociate the vaginal tissue from the rectum.
Cut the vagina off from the cervix to remove the vulva.
Incubate the vaginal tissue in 5 mL Dispase II mixture for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash the vaginal tissue with tissue isolation media.
Cut the vaginal tissue into small pieces.
Use sterile razor blades or scissors to cut the vaginal tissue.
Place the pieces into a 15-mL conical tube and fill the tube with tissue isolation media.
Centrifuge the 15-mL conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Incubate collected tissue pieces with the tissue digestion mixture.
Add 5 mL tissue digestion mixture to the tissue pieces.
Incubate the tissue pieces at 37°C for 30 min with 100 rpm shaking.
Neutralize the enzyme-treated tissue.
Add 5 mL enzyme neutralization media to the tube containing the vaginal tissue pieces and tissue digestion mixture.
Centrifuge the 15 mL conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Add 5 mL tissue isolation media.
Collect vaginal tissue cells containing vagina-infiltrated immune cells.
Place the 70-μm cell strainer on the 100 mm × 15 mm petri dish.
Put 5 mL tissue isolation media into the 70-μm cell strainer to soak the strainer before use.
Vortex the 15-mL conical tube and pour the tissue with tissue isolation media into the cell strainer.
Thoroughly grind the tissue pieces using the cell strainer and a plunger.
Attach the strainer on a 50 mL conical tube.
Pour the cell suspension collected in the petri dish into the strainer.
Wash the strainer with 5 mL tissue isolation media to collect residual cells.
Centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 1 mL Red blood cell lysis buffer and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 10 mL flow cytometry media to the cells and centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g, then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL T cell culture media.
Pass the resuspended cells through a sterilized 70-μm mesh to remove dead cell clumps.
Count the cell numbers and store the cells on wet ice until further use.
Transfer cell suspension into a FACS tube.
Add 2 mL flow cytometry media to the sample and centrifuge the FACS tube for 5 min at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat step to fully wash out the residual T cell culture media.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1–2 mL flow cytometry media to reach a final concentration of 1×10^6 cells/mL.
Add 5 μL (equal to 0.25 μg of chemical mass) 7-Amino-Actinomycin D per 1×10^6 cells and incubate for 5–10 min in the dark.
Sort 7-Amino-Actinomycin D negative immune cells using a FACSAria Fusion until obtaining 1–2 × 10^5 total cells.
Collect sorted cells with a new 15-mL conical tube containing 5 mL T cell culture media.
Fill the tube containing sorted cells with cold D-PBS up to 15 mL.
Centrifuge the FACS tube for 5 min at 400 × g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant without disrupting the cell pellet.
Repeat centrifugation and discard supernatant until residual T cell culture media is fully washed out.
Resuspend the cells with cold D-PBS to reach a final concentration of approximately 1000 cells/μL.
Proceed with cell barcoding following the manufacturer’s protocol for 10× Genomics.
Perform reverse transcription, fragmentation, end repair, A-tailing, adaptor ligation, library construction, and sequencing as per the manufacturer's guidelines.
Run 10× Chromium Cell Ranger according to the manufacturer’s protocol to generate barcodes (barcodes.tsv), features (features.tsv), and feature-barcode matrix (matrix.mtx).
Create Seurat objects and perform quality control.
Exclude cells with unique features of RNA where nFeature_RNA is less than 200 or greater than 6,000.
Exclude cells with more than 5% of reads aligning with mitochondrial genes during quality control.
Normalize the Seurat object as per standard procedures.
Find variable features in the normalized Seurat object.
Combine anchorsets by using FindIntegrationAnchors.
Integrate data using the IntegrateData function.
Perform scaling of the data using ScaleData.
Run principal component analysis using RunPCA.
Execute non-linear dimensional reduction with runUMAP.
Find neighbors for clustering using FindNeighbors, setting dims = 1:30.
Cluster cells using FindClusters, setting resolution = 0.5.
Plot clustered cells using DimPlot.
Re-cluster the T cell population.
Analyze the expression level of target molecules to identify γδ T cells.
Find differentially expressed genes in γδ T cells.
Put 1 × 10^6 cells into a FACS tube.
Add 2 mL flow cytometry media to the sample and centrifuge for 5 min at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat step to fully wash out the residual T cell culture media.
Add 100 μL flow cytometry media containing an Fc blocker diluted at a 1:100 ratio per million cells.
Incubate the cells for 20 min at 4°C.
Add 2 mL flow cytometry media to the sample and centrifuge for 5 min at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Keep the centrifuge temperature at 4°C.
Add 100 μL flow cytometry analysis antibody mixture to the cell pellet.
Vortex the FACS tube.
Incubate the cells for 20 min at 4°C.
Add 2 mL flow cytometry media to the sample.
Centrifuge the FACS tube for 5 min at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat the previous two steps if necessary.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL flow cytometry media.
Add 5 μL propidium iodide solution to the sample.
Incubate for 5 min.
Obtain .fcs data using BD LSRFortessa X-20 or other flow cytometers.
Export .fcs data and load it into FlowJo or other software.
Identify cell types and phenotypes of analyzed cells.
Prepare an anti-γδTCR antibody-coated 24-well plate.
Place 500 μl anti-γδTCR antibody coating solution into each well of a non-tissue culture-treated 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 4°C for 18–24 hours to coat the plate.
Aspirate the anti-γδTCR antibody coating solution before cell stimulation.
Harvest the spleen from C57BL/6J mice.
Place the harvested spleen on a 70 μm cell strainer placed over a petri dish filled with tissue isolation media.
Thoroughly grind the spleen to obtain single-cell suspension.
Collect the single-cell suspension outside of the cell strainer.
Put the strainer in a 50 mL conical tube.
Pour the cell suspension from the petri dish into the strainer.
Wash the strainer with 5 mL tissue isolation media to collect residual cells.
Centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Treat the harvested cells with Red blood cell lysis buffer.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 5 mL Red blood cell lysis buffer and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 45 mL flow cytometry media to the tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL magnetic sorting media.
Pass the resuspended cells through a sterilized 70-μm mesh to remove dead cell clumps.
Count cell numbers.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend 1 × 10^7 cells in 0.1 mL magnetic sorting media.
Place the cells in a 5-mL polystyrene tube.
Enrich γδ T cells.
Perform CD19+ cell depletion using a CD19-Positive Selection Kit and collect unbound cells.
Treat each 0.1 mL of cells (1 × 10^7 cells) with 20 μL MagniSort® Anti-Mouse CD19 Biotin and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Add 1 mL magnetic sorting media to the tube and centrifuge the conical tube for 5 min at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant and add 0.1 mL magnetic sorting media per 1 × 10^7 cells.
Treat each 0.1 mL of cells with 20 μL MagniSort® Positive Selection Beads and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Add up to 2.5 mL magnetic sorting media to the tube and insert the tube into the magnet.
Wait for 5 min to separate antibody-bound cells from unbound cells.
Pour the unbound cells into a new 50-mL conical tube to collect γδ T cell-containing cell suspension.
Count cells using trypan blue staining.
Collect 1 × 10^5 cells for analysis of sorting efficiency.
Perform CD4+ cell depletion using a CD4-Positive Selection Kit.
Collect unbound cells following the procedure described in step 53a.
Perform CD8+ cell depletion using a CD8-Positive Selection Kit.
Collect unbound cells following the procedure described in step 53a.
Collect 5 × 10^4 cells for the analysis of sorting efficiency.
Prepare T cell stimulation media by adding 1 μg/mL anti-CD28 antibody and 500 IU/mL recombinant human IL-2 to the T cell culture media.
Place 1 × 10^6 γδ T cell-enriched splenocytes and 1 mL T cell stimulation media into the antibody-coated 24-well plate.
Incubate cells in a humidified incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 48 hours for stimulation.
Subculture the cells.
Collect the cells.
Centrifuge the conical tube for 5 minutes at 400 × g and discard the supernatant.
Count the cell number.
Add T cell culture media to obtain 5 × 10^5 cells/mL with 500 IU/mL recombinant human IL-2.
Use flow cytometry to analyze γδ T cell expansion by measuring γδTCR+ cell proportion.
